_what: Every choice of the current run. FEATURES.md says what each means.

years._what: puf: the PUF's tax year (its records, cut points and dollar maps); target: the year of the file the tilt makes and of its targets (SOI, SCF wave, CEX year, non-filer pool).

paths._what: out: the scratch folder every stage writes under (common.py; REBUILD_OUT overrides it). raw: the input files, read only.

tax_units._what: The shared tax-unit rules (tax_units.py), run on every survey's member list (roster_cps.py, roster_scf.py, roster_cex.py). TAX_UNITS.md, section 4.
tax_units._reassign: CBO's reassignment pass (4c): true is CBO's default; false applies the first assignment only. The SCF and CEX (roster_scf.py, roster_cex.py) read it; the CPS's units (filing.py) follow cps.cbo_variant, 'cbo' (with the pass) or 'strict' (without), and tax_units.py run as a script takes --strict.
tax_units._npeu_split: The SCF's adults outside the primary economic unit: how the group's income is divided among them. equal: equally; moore: wages among those under 70 and Social Security and pensions among those 62 and over (Moore's rule). The group's balance sheet is divided equally either way.

network._what: The network (model.py, SlotTransformer): width of each slot's vector, layers, attention heads, ffn (the width inside each layer's feed-forward block), dropout.

training._what: Training (train.py): seed (REBUILD_SEED overrides it), passes over the table (REBUILD_PASSES overrides it), batch (records per step; 512 since 26 October, 4,096 before: about 1,780 steps a pass, an hour of training on an H100), the learning rate's peak, warm-up passes and final share of the peak, weight_decay, the share of the table held back to measure the fit (holdback_share, holdback_seed), and how often the log reports (log_every_passes).
training._precision: fp32 standard 32-bit; tf32 or bf16 cheaper formats for the training steps only (train.py). Tested 22 October (explore/2026-10-22/perf/precision/PRECISION.md): bf16 37% faster a pass, results within the difference between two seeds. bf16 since 26 October.
training._shares_shown_with_their_base: Step 2 (train.py, model.gate_shares): on CPS rows the spouse's share of the couple's wages (of its self-employment income) is left out of a record whenever married or the share's base is hidden, so its presence never tells the network what those hidden slots hold; needed to draw non-filers' married flag and amounts under the CPS label. false: as before step 2.
training._q_groups: Grouped weighting (qgroups.py, 26 October): each training record counts by its survey weight times q = records / weight within its group, the groups from bands: 12 band-AGI groups on the PUF (agi12), 5 band-income classes per wave on the SCF (income5); q = 1 on the CEX and CPS. null: q = 1 everywhere.
training._label_always_shown: On PUF rows the AGI group label is never hidden in training and never scored (train.py), as generation always presets it (TARGETS.md S8: $10M+ returns 3.3 times the PUF's with the label hidden half the time, 1.2 times with it always shown).
training._fillin_puf_side: The filers' share in the fill-in's formula (fillin.py): 'data', the PUF training rows' own survey-weighted shares by type (needed with grouped weighting, which tilts the network's answer toward the top AGI groups; the network's answer kept for types with fewer than 30 PUF records); 'model', the network's answer under the PUF label.

translation._what: Translation (translate.py): one row per survey and variable it shares with the PUF; a variable not here is not shared. Every comparison is against the tax data for the survey's year: PUF filers other than dependent filers, weights scaled by SOI Table 1.6 (filing status x age), dollars grown per return with the item, and the CPS units of that year (or the nearest CPS year) weighted by their chance of not filing. items: the survey's columns, summed; an empty list is zero (an item the survey does not ask). Definition fixes: first_year (asked from this tax year; earlier years zero), part (positive: the positive part; loss: the size of the loss, stored positive), loss_cap. loss_cap: a definition fix, losses read as no more than this. Function 1, dollar_line (PUF-year dollars, grown to the survey's year per return): amounts within the line of zero keep their dollars; amounts beyond it get the tax data's amount at the same count from the top (losses: from the bottom); null is dollars throughout, 0 is rank throughout. Function 2, fill_in (fillin.py): the two-slot fill-in on function 1's bands, with the size ranges where reporting rates are read; it conditions on the variables with type_for_fill_in (and the survey year), which cannot have it themselves. Default: dollars, no fill-in; a departure gives its reason. report_lines: the dollar lines (survey-year dollars) of the report's size ranges.

translation._cps_zero_in_tax_data: PUF amounts the CPS has no row for (absent on CPS rows) that the CPS units in the tax data carry as zero. interest (John, 23 October): the CPS has no interest item lined up with the PUF's taxable interest.

cex._what: The CEX interview survey as a third source (build_cex.R, build_table.py): survey years 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023 and 2024, one row per tax unit and quarterly interview; every tax unit trains, a shared household's spending divided by head count (build_cex.R); dependent filers are folded into the unit that claims them, and the file's own dependent filers get no consumption. The 8 consumption categories are CEX-only slots, drawn last at generation under the CEX label and generation_year; dollars from that year's records. Shared with the PUF: married, dependents, age range, wages, gross Social Security (ss_gross) and self-employment income. The tilt's consumption targets come from the target year's CEX, all tax units.

cps._what: The CPS ASEC as a fourth source (build_cps.R): TAX years (the ASEC of March of the next year), every tax unit of the household population by CBO's rules (tax_units.py, the shared tax-unit module) as the filing stage built them (filing.py), filers and non-filers; dependent filers folded into the unit that claims them. p_file (the table's filer_p) is the return's calibrated filing chance from the filing stage (its separate returns, filing status and statutory requirement come from there too); training draws the filing flag from it in every pass. filer is one draw from it, one uniform per unit seeded by filer_seed plus the year, kept for the table's checks and reports. generation_year: the CPS label's year at generation. The CPS-only slots (build_table.py, CPS_AMOUNTS and CPS_CATEGORIES): exact ages and sex of the primary filer and spouse, dependents' ages, the spouse's share of the couple's wages and of its self-employment income, weeks and usual hours worked, childcare; drawn last at generation under the CPS label and generation_year. dollar_amounts: the CPS-only amounts in dollars, grown from the generation year to the target year by SOI's wages per return.
cps._step1_dir: The filing stage's folder, inside the run's data folder (filing.py): the CPS's tax units and roster in <step1_dir>/units/ (roster_<year>_<cbo_variant>_nogq.csv.gz, which build_cps.R reads), the filing requirement in <step1_dir>/requirement/, the returns in <step1_dir>/<step1_out>/ and the checks in <step1_dir>/checks/. The name is from PLAN_v2.md's step 1, where the stage was built.
cps._step1_out: The folder inside step1_dir that holds the filing stage's returns (units_<year>.csv.gz, one row per return, separate returns included, with the calibrated filing chance p_file_cal), which build_cps.R reads.

filing._what: The CPS's filing stage (filing.py, filing_requirement.R; run.sbatch stage filing): every CPS tax unit's chance of filing, by the filing rule v4 (John, 24 October 2026): logit(chance) = a(age band of the head) + k x (a child under 17) + required x (r + s x log gross income, centred on the year's weighted median among required units + b x (business or farm income not zero)), required being the statutory filing requirement. The 11 settings (7 a's, k, r, s, b) are solved each year so that 11 targets hold exactly: non-filing heads and spouses in 7 age bands = CPS adults - adults on returns (SOI Table 1.6, age_shape's filing_adults) - dependents aged 15+ not filing their own return (group quarters left out, so zero); and the four shares below. Dependents' own returns: file if required to or with any wages. No outside filing model.
filing._child_share: Non-filing children under 17 as a share of the CPS's children under 17, every year: the 2015 share, (Census PEP under 17, 69,494,950, less the 2015 PUF's N24 on returns other than dependent filers, 67,354,355.8) / 69,494,950 = 2,140,594.2 / 69,494,950. Child credit counts are not used after 2015 because the age limit, the Social Security number rule and refundability changed (John, 23 October 2026).
filing._required_nonfiling_share: Non-filing household units among units required to file, every year: 11.19 million (Pub 5785 Table 3, required non-filing units, TY2014-16 average; research/state_weights/nonfiler_residual/resources/pub5785_table3_notfiler_units.csv) / 118.53 million required units in the 2015 CPS (by this stage's units and requirement). The 2015 run checks the ratio.
filing._income_share: The gross income of required non-filers as a share of all required units' gross income, every year: $409.4 billion (Pub 5785 Table 3, total income of required non-filers, TY2014-16 average) / $8,987.5 billion (required units' gross income, 2015 CPS). The 2015 run checks the ratio.
filing._business_share: Required non-filers with business or farm income (head and spouse, INCBUS + INCFARM, positive or negative) as a share of required non-filers, every year: 4.99 / 11.19 million (Pub 5785 Table 3, TY2014-16 average).
filing._mfs_salt: Separate returns: joint couples are taken in the order of a uniform keyed by unit id with this salt (tax_units.mfs_split) until weight x calibrated chance reaches SOI Table 1.6's separate returns / 2.
filing._age_shape: Adults on returns by age band (column filing_adults: SOI Pub 1304 Table 1.6 as the non-filer pool's residual anchor builds it) and Census PEP adults (pep_adults, used only in a check), per year; tracked in the repository.
filing._pep_children: Census PEP resident population under 17 and under 18 on 1 July of each tax year, the national sum of the state rows (SEX 0, ORIGIN 0, all races): 2015, 2017 and 2019 from the 2010-2020 intercensal estimates (sc-est2020int-alldata6.csv), 2021 and 2023 from Vintage 2024 (sc-est2024-alldata6.csv), both in /nfs/roberts/project/pi_nrs36/shared/raw_data/Census-PEP/ (manifest.csv gives the Census URLs). Used in the checks only (people by age, and the children's row of nonfilers_vs_targets).

ages._what: The primary filer's age range (ages.py). Step 0 for PUF records with no range: a logit prior from the return, calibrated to SOI Table 1.6 less the known-range weight in each filing status x AGI cell where at least min_missing_share of the weight has no range. Survey couples: the man is the primary, except the woman with a chance by the man's range that reproduces the PUF's female-primary share by range; same-sex couples, the older partner.

generation._what: The filer batch and the non-filer batch (generate.py says how). design: 'label' (26 October), the AGI group label preset on every filer record and everything else drawn given it.
generation._label: label_records: the filer records over all pooled models (each draws an equal share), split across the 12 band-AGI groups (qgroups.py) in proportion to the PUF's records per group (about 18,400 at p99.99 and over, 30,500 at p99.9-99.99). Each record's group is preset; its weight is the group's 2015 PUF returns over the records drawn in it (1 / q). Every drawn record is kept; the share whose drawn bands fall in another group is only reported (label_check.csv). label_seed: the batch's draws (plus each model's seed_shift).
generation._scf_wave_seed: TARGETS.md section 7: each record's SCF wave is drawn with the shares in the target year's configuration (targets_config/years/<year>.yaml, prior, 'balance sheet'), by a random generator seeded by this and the batch's generation seed, so no other draw moves.
generation._nonfiler_records: Step 2: the non-filer batch, drawn from the CPS label at the target year with the filing flag 0, no oversampling, every weight 1. null: its number of records is the filer batch's (label_records) times the CPS's expected non-filers in the target year (sum of weight x (1 - filer_p)) over SOI's returns that year; a number fixes it. nonfiler_seed fixes its draws.
generation._models: The trained models pooled into each year's file (TARGETS.md section 8): equal shares of every batch, each model with its own generation seeds (seed_shift added to every seed), record ids from k x 10,000,000 for model k. Train each with REBUILD_RUN set to its run name (and REBUILD_SEED to its seed). null draws from the run's own model alone, with today's seeds; set it to null for a fresh single-seed train-then-generate run.

consistency._what: Consistency rules at generation: when any item in when_any_nonzero is nonzero on the record, at least one holding in then_at_least_one_nonzero must be nonzero (generate.py says how). offset_generations: how many times generation runs; after each run but the last, each ruled holding's odds of being nonzero are scaled by one factor so that, with the rules, its expected holders equal the model's own. 1 means no offset.

rules.name: a partnership or S corporation item

dollars._what: seed: the seed of the draws that pick each record's dollars within its drawn band from the dollar map (dollars.py).

tilt._what: Post-training (tilt.py, solver.py, TARGETS.md): the start's weights scaled, then the smallest Kullback-Leibler move of the weights that puts every target in the year's list (targets_config/, expanded by target_list.py, each with its standard error from errors.py) inside its range. Which targets, their values and their errors are in targets_config/, not here.
tilt._nonfiler_targets_dir: Inside the run's data folder: the filing stage's checks (filing.py), <year>_nonfilers_vs_targets.csv, column target_heads_spouses.
tilt._prescale: The default start_scaling weights, when the year file gives none (target_list.start_spec): 'demographic' (TARGETS.md section 4): filers scaled to SOI's returns, then to Table 1.2's joint and non-joint returns, then to Table 1.6's returns by age range in each, and non-filers to the CPS's expected non-filers, then to the non-filer people targets, before the tilt; 'filing_status' stops after the joint and non-joint returns; 'none' scales filers and non-filers to their totals only.
tilt._range_in_se: TARGETS.md S6: each non-identity target is met anywhere within its value plus or minus this many standard errors, at no cost inside the range (solver.py). 0 hits every target exactly. The number for every kind of target not in range_in_se_by_kind, and for the demographic prescaling. Half a standard error for every target was tested on 26 October (TARGETS.md S6): 23 targets (non-filer people bands against CEX food and health averages) could not all be met and the effective sample kept fell to 31%.
tilt._range_in_se_by_kind: TARGETS.md S9 (approved by John, 26 October): the range in standard errors by kind of target ({kind: k}, the kinds of targets_config/), so the SCF targets are held to half a standard error and every other kind to range_in_se. tilt.py turns it into one number per target for the solver; a kind named here with no targets in the year's list is an error. Empty ({}) or absent: range_in_se for every target, as before.
tilt._scf_target_waves: TARGETS.md S9: which SCF waves the SCF targets (kinds wealth and wealth grid) are computed on (scf_targets.py). 'prior': the year's mix, the year file's prior "balance sheet", the same waves and shares generation draws the balance sheet from (2019: the 2019 wave 54.65%, 2022 33.15%, 2016 12.20%); each wave's balance sheet grown per tax unit to the target year's wave as the maps are, its own lines; value = sum of share x the wave's value, variance = sum of share^2 x the wave's variance. 'target year': the target year's wave alone, for checks.

errors._what: Standard errors (errors.py, TARGETS.md section 9). Every setting here is optional, with the default given; none is set today.
errors._scf_replicate_dir: The folder of each SCF wave's replicate weights (p<yy>_rw1.dta, from the Federal Reserve; errors.py says how to fetch them), with {wave} in the path for the wave. Default: <out>/data/scf_rw/{wave}, which holds the 2016, 2019 and 2022 waves' files. Every wave in a year's mix needs its folder (scf_targets.py).
errors._other: soi_cv_dir (default <out>/targets/soi_cv), borrow_neighbours (5), full_sample_se (0.01), nonfiler_count_se (0.06), nonfiler_people_population_se (0.005), definition_gap ({}): errors.py's docstring says what each means.
